source: ACIAR Monograph No. 146a, "ដំណាំសំណែកសៀង" [Soybean Growers Manual], Belfield S., Brown C., Martin M. (eds.), New South Wales Department of Primary Industries / Murdoch University / CARDI / ACIAR, 2012
text:
This ACIAR Monograph No. 146a "Soybean Growers Manual" (2012) is the most comprehensive source in this batch — a full 76-page technical manual produced through New South Wales Department of Primary Industries, Murdoch University, CARDI, and ACIAR collaboration (building on ACIAR projects ASEM/2000/109 and ASEM/2006/130).

It opens with an introduction to soybean (Glycine max) as a legume oilseed of global importance, tracing rapid growth in world production from 2000–2005 and noting soybean's economic importance to Cambodia specifically, with a chart of Cambodian soybean planted-area trends from roughly 1980–2007 showing strong growth into the mid-2000s followed by fluctuation. National production statistics are cited: around 43,000 ha planted, yielding roughly 4.0–6.7 t/ha of unmilled rice-equivalent comparison crops nearby, with soybean's own average national yield cited distinctly lower than research-station yields, and the manual gives a bar chart comparing average farmer yield, yield with recommended inputs, on-station trial yield, world average yield, and a target/aspirational yield for Cambodia (values roughly 1.5, 3.4, 3.8, 1.6, 4.0 t/ha respectively across those categories) making the point that a large yield gap exists between current farmer practice and achievable yield.
